chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who goes out for hunting, should he shorten [the prayer] or complete [it]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete [the prayer], because it is not a rightful travel.'

key_terms.مَسِيرِ حَقٍّ: Rightful travel (a journey for a valid purpose like trade, pilgrimage, or war, which qualifies for shortening prayers)
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: Complete the prayer (praying four rak'ahs as in normal conditions)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: Shorten the prayer (praying two rak'ahs instead of four during travel)

ai.seo_question: Should a person shorten their prayers when traveling for hunting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that hunting is classified as a leisure journey rather than a 'rightful travel' (safar haqq), thereby requiring the traveler to perform complete (tamm) prayers. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the permissibility of shortening prayers depends on the purpose of the journey, excluding recreational activities from the concession granted to travelers.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who goes out to the hunting (for leisure), should he shorten or pray complete?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should pray complete because it is not a rightful travel’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who goes for hunting. Can he perform his Salah (prayer) as reduced? He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to perform his Salah (prayer) as complete, because it is not a journey in the way of truth.’”
